solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go off vehicle used by independent mum

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
'mum' as in keep mum, be quiet: SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A mother gets a van with her own money and drives off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother, but it is the old word for silence, as in 'mum's the word', so it gives SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off can mean to disappear from view, which is to vanish.

clue.text: Confirm I had a brief time in glen

indicators.note: the contraction and the other pieces go inside the valley

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a glen
I had contracts to I'D
T is the abbreviation for time, a brief form of it

explanation.surface: Someone confirms they spent a short spell in a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To validate something is to confirm that it is correct or genuine.

clue.text: Shock intelligence about new place

indicators.note: the word for intelligence goes around the other pieces

parts.note: nous is common sense, intelligence
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Someone clever is shocked by a new place.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is British informal for common sense or practical intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to bewilder or shock them so they don't know how to react.

clue.text: What this rugby player demands? Namely, spirit and quantity of beer, perhaps

parts.note: SC stands for scilicet, Latin for namely
rum is a spirit
a half is half a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A rugby player orders a rum and half a pint of beer after the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces spell out his drinks order, SC + RUM + HALF: 'What ... demands?' frames the wordplay as what he might order at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrum-half is the rugby player who feeds the ball into the scrum.

clue.text: Team's method is a distraction

parts.note: a side is a team, so 'team's' gives SIDE'S, written without the apostrophe
how something is done is its method

explanation.surface: A coach complains that the team's way of playing is putting people off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a minor attraction that draws attention away from the main event.

clue.text: Current detained party may be wheeled out here

definitions.text: Current detained party may be wheeled out here

parts.words: Current detained party may be wheeled out here
parts.note: a suspect in custody is brought out to stand in a line of people for witnesses to pick out

explanation.surface: A political party now held may be brought out for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, but it is the person held, the suspect, who is wheeled out to be viewed by a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-up of people where a witness tries to pick out a suspect held by police.

clue.text: Time to absorb Times and Telegraph's first special edition

indicators.note: the period takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an era is a period of time
X is the multiplication sign, times

indicators.note: the first of the word Telegraph's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The Times and the Telegraph rush out a special edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign X. 'to absorb' puts X + T inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a special edition of a newspaper, printed for breaking news.

clue.text: Dangerous load carried under end of arch

indicators.note: in a down clue the load sits below the letter, following it
the end of the word arch is its final letter

parts.note: an armful is a load carried in the arms

explanation.surface: A heavy burden carried beneath an arch is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful means causing damage or injury, so dangerous.

clue.text: Poor figure — crone — about to replace one

indicators.note: the word for about takes the place of the numeral in the old woman

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman, a witch
I is the Roman numeral one
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sad character, an old hag, is about to be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'going to', but 'about' gives RE, which replaces the I (one) in WITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is an unfortunate or pitiful person, a poor figure.

clue.text: Feature of many a pub upsetting to barman indeed

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something in many pubs really annoys the barman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' looks like distressing the barman, but it signals the letters of TO BARMAN INDEED rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is a fruit machine, a slot machine once common in pubs.

clue.text: Extended left side of pitch by manor-house

parts.note: in cricket the on side (leg side) is one half of the field
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: A cricket ground is extended down its left side as far as the big house.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the ON side, so 'side of pitch' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range describes something with a great reach, so it is extended in distance or time.

clue.text: Bag containing initial slice of rich cake

indicators.note: the bag holds the next piece within it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a tote is a large bag

indicators.note: the first slice of the word rich is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bag holds the first slice of a rich cake to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of central European origin.

clue.text: Problem article from the Sorbonne blocking underpowered graduate

indicators.note: the article stands in the way of the other pieces, sitting inside them

parts.note: a dim light is underpowered
the Sorbonne is in Paris, so a French article: LE
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A French lecture holds up a feeble graduate student.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sorbonne is a Paris university, so the article wanted is a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between two options, a kind of problem.

clue.text: Instant cut involving air service following illegal trading

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps around the other pieces, taking them in
the word for an instant is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tick is an instant, as in 'just a tick'
the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A sudden ban on flights is brought in after smuggling is discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' reads as a link word joining wordplay to definition, but it supplies a letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic in goods is to deal in them illegally, as in drug trafficking.

clue.text: Scientist fully prepared to return, abandoning last student

indicators.note: the final L of the turned-round letters is given up
the phrase meaning ready is read back to front

parts.note: all set means completely ready
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: A researcher, all ready to come back, leaves the last pupil behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns ALLSET into TESLLA, and 'abandoning last' drops its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the inventor and engineer who pioneered alternating current.

clue.text: Postpone aeroplane yarn?

parts.note: the de Havilland Moth, such as the Tiger Moth, is a classic aeroplane
yarn is wound into a ball

explanation.surface: A question asks whether a story about a plane should be put off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale to go with the plane, but it is the wool, wound in a BALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To mothball a plan is to shelve it for later, as clothes are stored with mothballs.

clue.text: About to engage in assault after line's encouragement to attack

indicators.note: the letter for about is set into the other letters
the line letter is set into the assault, coming after its first four letters

parts.note: battery is physical assault, as in assault and battery
L is the abbreviation for line
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A rallying call to attack follows the line about to engage in an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts L into BATTERY to give BATTLERY, and 'to engage in' then puts C after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle cry is a shout used to rouse troops when they charge.

clue.text: Satisfied husband with an unfinished vintage spirit

parts.note: met as in met a demand, satisfied it

indicators.note: the word for vintage loses its last letter

parts.note: vintage means old

explanation.surface: A contented husband shares a vintage spirit he hasn't quite finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like a drink, but this one is chemical, a type of alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Methanol is methyl alcohol, also called wood spirit.

clue.text: Exhausted and through with an exalted self-image

parts.note: puffed means out of breath, exhausted
finished, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: Someone worn out and finished still thinks very highly of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone puffed up is conceited, swollen with their own importance.

clue.text: Free to bring in Republican that's inexperienced

indicators.note: the word for free takes in the letter for Republican

parts.note: untied means released, free

explanation.surface: A newcomer is freed to bring in a Republican with no experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring in' puts R inside UNTIED, after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Untried means not yet tested, so lacking experience.

clue.text: Start to triumph in element of Scrabble championship

indicators.note: the opening letter goes inside the Scrabble piece

parts.note: Scrabble is played with letter tiles

indicators.note: the start of the word triumph is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A player's first win comes in a Scrabble championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T inside TILE, after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a championship won in a sport, as in a world title.

clue.text: What teachers offer, I note, abandoning sense

indicators.note: the two letters leave the word for sense

parts.note: intuition is a sense, a hunch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher notes that sense is being left out of lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes IN, the I and N of the clue, from the front of INTUITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, which is what teachers give.

clue.text: Lots dismissing new border chaos

indicators.note: the word for lots sends away the letter for new

parts.note: many means lots
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Many people sacked and a new frontier cause disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder, total chaos.

clue.text: Island trying to dispose of seagull droppings? No no

parts.note: anyone against something wants rid of it, so anti

indicators.note: here meaning 'without', so the word that follows is taken away

parts.note: guano is the droppings of seabirds

explanation.surface: Someone on an island campaigns to clean up the gull mess, and gets told no.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTI + GUANO would be anti-guano; 'No no' means without NO, removing the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Nobbled board-game? Rubbish

parts.note: Go is an ancient board game from East Asia
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A rigged board game is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To get at someone is to bribe or interfere with them, which is what nobbling means.

clue.text: Explorer just stopping short, interrupted by porter?

indicators.note: the beer breaks into the shortened word
the word for fair loses its final letter

parts.note: right means just or fair
porter is a dark beer, so ale

explanation.surface: An explorer halts just short of his goal, having been interrupted by a luggage carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like someone carrying bags, but porter is also a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer of the Americas.

clue.text: That chap's tense about international criminal operation

indicators.note: the contraction for 'he is' goes around the next letter

parts.note: that chap is HE, so 'that chap's' is HE'S
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A man is nervous about an international crime job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside HE'S to make HEIS, and T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially a carefully planned one.

clue.text: One's worked out amount of tax?

definitions.meaning: a conclusion worked out by reasoning
an amount taken off, as tax is deducted from pay

explanation.surface: An accountant has calculated how much tax is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deduction is both reasoning to a conclusion and a sum subtracted, such as tax from pay.

clue.text: Think it's included in medicine consumed orally?

indicators.note: the word it is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: eaten by mouth: ate
it is the word it, taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient wonders whether the pill should be swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply or contemplate.

clue.text: Collection of religious songs gutted holy men most of all

indicators.note: with their insides removed, the two words keep only their outer letters
most of the word all keeps everything but its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Holy men emptied of feeling sing most of all from a book of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns, which are religious songs.
